newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA TELL BOSNICH HIS PLACE IS SECURE -- FOR NOW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA TELL BOSNICH HIS PLACE IS SECURE -- FOR NOW.

text.p: Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich has been told his first team place is safe for now even though he is under investigation by the police and Football Association after his Nazi-style salute.
Australian Bosnich incensed Tottenham supporters -- many of whom are Jewish -- with his actions during the second half of Saturday's premier league match at White Hart Lane.
He could face disciplinary action from the F.A., while the Metropolitan Police are continuing to review the incident after receiving many complaints from Spurs fans.
"We will have to wait and see what the F.A. and police decide to do, but it won't affect Bosnich's situation with Aston Villa. He will continue to play for us," Villa manager Brian Little said.V
"Mark was trying to have a bit of fun with the crowd but didn't make a very good job of it.
"Having seen a picture of what happened, you can see that what he genuinely felt was funny certainly isn't."
Little declined to say whether the club would take their own action against Bosnich who was playing his first match of the season after a knee problem.

Bosnich turned and gave the salute to the Tottenham fans who had bated him throughout the match for an incident 18 months ago when he knocked then Spurs German striker Juergen Klinsmann unconscious in a rash challenge.
Bosnich rang a radio soccer call-in programme on Saturday night to apologise for his action after many callers rang in to give their opinion on the matter.

But it may not save him from punishment -- if not by the police, then almost certainly the F.A. whose spokesman Steve Double said: "It is not a trivial matter and caused offence to a great number of people."
